extracted.intended_audience: petitioners seeking nonregulated status (biotech firms), regulated parties, and the interested public (stakeholders, commenters, and regulatory/legal professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards used by USDA APHIS to evaluate a petition seeking a determination of nonregulated status for a genetically engineered organism under 7 CFR part 340, including use of a Plant Pest Risk Assessment (PPRA), consideration of public comments, and applicable statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Determination of Nonregulated Status (§ 340.6(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations in § 340.6(a) provide that any person may submit a petition to the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) seeking a determination that an article should not be regulated under 7 CFR part 340.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must provide information in support of the position that the organism is unlikely to pose a plant pest risk. APHIS evaluates information and data submitted in the petition, available scientific data, the plant pest risk assessment (PPRA), and public comments received. (Referenced: 'The petition provides information in support of the position that MON 95379 is unlikely to pose a plant pest risk and therefore should not be regulated under APHIS' regulations in 7 CFR part 340.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Pest Risk Assessment (PPRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: APHIS prepares a plant pest risk assessment (PPRA) to assess the plant pest risk of the organism; a draft PPRA was published for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft PPRA is published in the Federal Register and opened for public comment (dates provided). The final PPRA is used in APHIS' evaluation and supports the determination. (Referenced: 'As part of our decision-making process ... APHIS prepared a draft plant pest risk assessment (PPRA) to assess the plant pest risk of the organism.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative plant pest risk standard for nonregulated status
rubrics_metrics.description: An organism is determined to be no longer subject to regulation if it is 'unlikely to pose a greater plant pest risk than the unmodified comparator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APHIS's determination is explicitly based on evaluation in the final PPRA of information and data submitted in the petition, available scientific data, and public comments. The finding that the organism is 'unlikely to pose a greater plant pest risk than the unmodified comparator' is the substantive standard for removing regulatory status. (Referenced: 'Based on APHIS’ evaluation in the final PPRA ... APHIS has determined that MON 95379 is unlikely to pose a greater plant pest risk than the unmodified comparator and therefore is no longer subject to our regulation ...')

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment process and consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft assessments (e.g., draft PPRA) are published and opened for public comment for stated periods; APHIS considers public comments in its evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: APHIS published the draft PPRA in the Federal Register and accepted public comments from June 3, 2025, through July 3, 2025, receiving 594 comments. APHIS provides a response to comments document and uses comments, together with data and scientific literature, in making its determination. (Referenced: 'APHIS published the draft PPRA ... and accepted public comments ... APHIS received five hundred ninety-four comments.' and 'Copies of the signed determination, final PPRA, and response to comments ... are available ...')

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA practice / Environmental Assessment (EA) update
rubrics_metrics.description: APHIS announced a Program Update that it will no longer prepare a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) analysis (environmental assessment) to accompany its review of petitions seeking a determination of nonregulated status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the Program Update (dated July 9, 2025), APHIS terminated work on the EA for this petition. This is a procedural change affecting how environmental analyses accompany petition reviews. (Referenced: 'In this Program Update, APHIS announced that it will no longer prepare a National Environmental Policy Act analysis ... Therefore, consistent with this July 9, 2025 Program Update, APHIS terminated work on the EA.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and transparency of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the signed determination, final PPRA, response to comments, and the previously published petition and supporting documents are made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents are accessible via Regulations.gov (docket APHIS-2020-0113), the Federal eRulemaking Portal, the agency reading room, and the official PDF on govinfo.gov. The notice provides contact information and reading-room procedures. (Referenced: 'Copies of the signed determination, final PPRA, and response to comments, as well as the previously published petition and supporting documents, are available as indicated in the ADDRESSES ...')

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and statutory/regulatory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations are made under the authority of the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7701 et seq.) and regulations in 7 CFR part 340, along with other cited statutory/regulatory authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice cites specific authorities (7 U.S.C. 7701-7772 and 7781-7786; 31 U.S.C. 9701; 7 CFR 2.22, 2.80, and 371.3) to ground APHIS' regulatory action. Compliance with these statutes and regulations is the legal framework for petitions and determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of regulatory status change
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice states the date on which the change in regulatory status is recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this determination, the change in regulatory status is recognized as of September 24, 2025. Such dates are provided in notices to establish when regulatory obligations change.
